segments.he: וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ פָּטוּר. רַב הוּנָא מַתְנֵי חַיָּיב, וּמוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּדוּקִין שֶׁבְּעַיִן, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר: אִם עָלוּ לֹא יֵרְדוּ.
segments.en: It is stated: «And one who slaughters them outside» the Temple courtyard is «exempt» from karet. The Gemara notes: «Rav Huna taught» this as: One who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard «is liable» to receive karet, «and he interprets it» as referring to a case involving an animal with a minor blemish, such as «on the cornea of the eye. And» the mishna is «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rabbi Akiva, who says:» Although animals with a minor blemish may not be sacrificed ab initio, «if they ascended» the altar «they shall not descend» and are sacrificed. Since an animal with a minor blemish is potentially suitable for sacrifice, one who slaughters it outside the Temple courtyard is liable to receive karet.
